papers.title: A framework for linking literature-based knowledge integration and infrastructure-supported knowledge integration: Opportunities and challenges from a case study
papers.abstract: Integrating knowledge across disciplines is central to sustainability research, yet most evidence-synthesis methods rely on findings as reported in publications, limiting verification and reuse of underlying data and workflows. We develop a conceptual framework linking literature-based and infrastructure-supported knowledge integration, using a systematic review case study to examine when integration can extend beyond reported findings. We reviewed 37 studies on climate change, violent conflict, and household food security. Literature-based synthesis enabled integration across all included studies, whereas access to reusable outputs was limited: over half provided no data availability statement, 27% reported availability upon request, but reusable data and workflows were available for only 8%. To explore infrastructure-supported integration, we used the TIB Knowledge Loom to represent studies with accessible data and code as machine-readable outputs, and produced a knowledge gap map (KGM) from manually extracted and Loom-derived data, comparing manual and infrastructure-supported synthesis. Where outputs were reusable, synthesis could be produced directly from data and workflows rather than from publications. These findings show that literature-based synthesis can be complemented by infrastructure-supported integration where outputs are accessible and usable, and that advancing knowledge integration depends not only on infrastructures but on making data, code, and workflows accessible, executable, and reusable.

papers.title: PublicnEUro: A FAIR and TRUSTworthy infrastructure for controlled access to human neuroimaging data
papers.abstract: Sharing brain imaging data supports secondary analysis and reproducibility, but privacy risks and differing legal and governance requirements can make unrestricted release inappropriate. The PublicnEUro repository was developed to support discovery and reuse under diverse legal requirements. Here, PublicnEUro's governance, architecture, BIDS-based deposition and curation, metadata and identifier services as well as open and controlled retrieval workflows are described. We then assess the repository published datasets against FAIR subprinciples and the repository public information against TRUST principles. The FAIR assessment shows strong findability and public metadata accessibility. The TRUST assessment documents governance, stewardship, continuity provisions and technical safeguards. Together this demonstrates that PublicnEUro, by separating open discovery from governed data retrieval, supports FAIR-aligned and trustworthy reuse of sensitive brain imaging data without requiring unrestricted disclosure.

papers.title: The FlightFinder Occurrence Corpus: harmonising 128 aviation-safety source codes into one deduplicated cross-national accident dataset
papers.abstract: National aviation-investigation databases are deep but territorial; global compilations such as the Aviation Safety Network and the Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives are hand-curated, apply their own inclusion thresholds, and publish no field-level lineage. The FlightFinder Occurrence Corpus harmonizes 279,485 occurrences and 131,882 attached narratives from 128 source codes - national accident-investigation authorities, occurrence-reporting systems and four global compilations. Records are mapped into one schema; apart from a duplicate pre-filter on three sources, each normalized record reduces to exactly one key from an ordered ladder - event signature, registration and date, rounded position and date, or source and native identifier - so a missing field never creates a link, and the key is the occurrence identifier. Records the ladder cannot reach are scored in a blocked pass into an explicit merge table and applied only within an automatically approved score band or after a person confirms them. Field conflicts follow a documented source ranking; one provenance row per contributing source - its record identifier and URL - is retained, with attribution and licence terms per source code. Linkage error is measured on five adjudicated samples totalling 200 pairs. A recorded uniform random draw of 60 from the 3,441 merges the automatic band applies as it ships found no error; the exact two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on its false-merge rate is 6.0%, or 205 pairs. The measured error covers the scored band only; the ladder's deterministic joins are not adjudicated. The corpus has no exposure denominators and inherits the under-reporting of its sources. It is offered as a base for cross-national safety statistics, source-disagreement studies and narrative text mining; a frozen, DOI-referenced snapshot accompanies the live API.
